title: genai scorer serialization: a new persisted timeout field must reload legacy scorers as 0, not the new default
answers: After upgrading MLflow, my already-registered scorers suddenly time out. Why?
Why does a freshly created scorer serialize timeout as None but a reloaded old scorer comes back as 0?
How do I add a new option to a registered scorer without changing behavior for existing monitoring jobs?
Where is the scorer timeout saved and reloaded during registration?
body:
Path: Scorer persistence goes through `mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py:Scorer.model_dump` into `SerializedScorer`, and back through `Scorer._reconstruct_decorator_scorer` (and `Scorer.model_validate`) when a registered scorer is loaded for evaluate or online monitoring.
Rule: `SerializedScorer.timeout` defaults to `0` so a payload missing the key reloads as unbounded, the legacy behavior; `Scorer.timeout` defaults to `None`, so only freshly created scorers get `DEFAULT_SCORER_TIMEOUT`. When adding a field to `SerializedScorer`, choose the default that reproduces pre-existing behavior for old payloads and set the new default only on the in-memory object.
Symptom: Without this split, scorers registered before the change would have started being bounded at 300s on reload, failing long-running judge calls in existing monitoring workloads.
Constraints: Tests in `tests/genai/scorers/test_serialization.py` pin this (a payload with the `timeout` key deleted reloads to `0`). This applies to the serialized form only; it does not change how an explicitly set `timeout` round-trips.
applies: Serialization and deserialization of `@scorer` / `Scorer` objects, including any new field added to `SerializedScorer`.
says: Existing registered evaluators suddenly time out on long tasks after an upgrade.
Production LLM judge monitoring jobs fail with timeout errors after updating.
Previously saved scorers should remain unbounded instead of timing out at five minutes.
Long-running evaluation jobs crash from unexpected timeouts on legacy registered judges.
Older evaluation scorers fail during monitoring because a default time limit was applied.
search: When serializing scorers in `mlflow.genai.scorers.base`, `SerializedScorer.timeout` defaults to `0` to keep legacy stored payloads unbounded, while in-memory `Scorer.timeout` defaults to `None` so only newly created scorers receive `DEFAULT_SCORER_TIMEOUT`. When loading registered scorers for evaluation or online monitoring via `Scorer._reconstruct_decorator_scorer` and `Scorer.model_validate`, missing timeout keys reload as `0` instead of imposing a 300-second limit. When adding any new persisted field to `SerializedScorer`, default values must preserve pre-existing behavior for older serialized payloads while applying new defaults solely to fresh in-memory objects. This constraint applies strictly to the serialized schema format and does not alter round-tripping for explicitly defined timeouts.
